\begin{minipage}{0.95\linewidth}\vspace{4pt}\scriptsize \textit{Notes:} All rows except the last two: T3 specification (growth of real GDP per capita, five-year averages, wage bill in t\_p $-$ 1, controls in t\_p $-$ 1, country and period fixed effects) in the T3 sample, with the variable named in the row added. Output gap: 100 $\times$ (log real GDP $-$ Hamilton trend, H = 2, k = 2) in t\_p $-$ 1. Growth of p $-$ 1: lagged five-year average growth (LSDV, Nickell bias not corrected); rows with it lose the first period of each country. Negative-gap rows: the wage-bill coefficient after a positive gap, the interaction, and their sum. 2SLS: the ratio in t\_p $-$ 1 instrumented by the annual ratios in t\_p $-$ 2 and t\_p $-$ 3, country and period fixed effects, T3 controls, standard errors clustered by country; WRE wild bootstrap. Bootstrap: wild cluster bootstrap by country, Webb weights, 9,999 replications (p for T3 differs slightly from Table A9 because the bootstrap seed differs). T3, same observations: T3 re-estimated on the observations of the row. Annual rows: Table 1 model (1996--2023, controls of Table 1, country and year fixed effects) with the ratio in t $-$ 1 over Hamilton trend GDP in t $-$ 1; coefficient with wild cluster bootstrap by country. Gelbach (2016): contribution of each added variable to the change in the wage-bill coefficient, standard errors clustered by country. γ $\times$ δ: product of the within regressions of growth in p and of the ratio in t\_p $-$ 1 on growth in p $-$ 1 (country and period fixed effects); γ\_long $\times$ π: the coefficient on growth of p $-$ 1 in T3 + growth of p $-$ 1 times the coefficient of the wage bill in a regression of growth of p $-$ 1 on the wage bill and the T3 controls, which equals the observed change; 95\% intervals from a country-pairs bootstrap (999 replications). Exploratory (post-plan, pre-registered in the second plan addendum).\end{minipage}
